blocks.content: Function prototype provides information for the function name, return type, and data type of arguments.
It allows us to call functions before defining them.
Variables defined inside a function are local to it. It doesn't exist outside the function.

C++ provides various built-in functions that we can directly use in our program. We need to import the appropriate header file (such as cmath, cctype, etc.) to utilize most of these standard functions.

items: Helps to divide a large program into smaller chunks so that it's easier to write and understand.
Makes our code reusable. Once a function is defined, we can use it multiple times. We just need to call it.
Makes our code modular. We can use other programmers' functions if we know what arguments the function takes and what value it returns.
